elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New Article XII-A says only "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to Licensee's affiliates. By contrast the retained Article XII expressly requires Licensee to "defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A runs in favour of "Licensee" only; no extension to Licensee's affiliates, directors, officers, employees or agents (the mirror of what Article XII gives Licensor).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right", and the carve-out inserted in Article XIII(a) removes the retained bar on Licensor infringement liability.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no limb covering Licensor's breach of applicable law was added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb addressing unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee data caused by Licensor appears in Article XII-A or elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no gross negligence / wilful misconduct limb, and the Article XIII(a) carve-out is limited to "LICENSOR'S INDEMNITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A" (i.e. IP only).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic is inserted; Article XII-A moves straight from the indemnity to the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A is silent on who controls or settles the defence of an indemnified claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII is retained verbatim and remains broad: Licensee is "solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability" from exercising the licence and indemnifies for (i) exercise of the licence rights, (ii) conduct of Licensee's business, and (iii) any breach of the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"; the Article XIII(a) carve-out ("EXCEPT FOR LICENSOR'S INDEMNITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A") disapplies the retained no-infringement-liability bar so the obligation is operative.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: "excluding any claim arising from (i) modifications to the Licensed Technology made by Licensee".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: "(ii) combination of the Licensed Technology with items not supplied by Licensor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall procure for Licensee the right to continue using, or shall modify or replace, the affected Licensed Technology" — stated as a mandatory obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is available, Licensor shall refund the fees paid by Licensee for the affected Licensed Technology".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Licensor's aggregate liability under this Article XII-A shall not exceed three times the annual fees paid by Licensee under this Agreement", and the Article XIII(b) carve-out prevents the retained one-half-of-amounts-paid cap from swallowing the super-cap.

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Duplicate of the first preferred element; unchanged assessment — no defence obligation and no affiliate beneficiaries in Article XII-A.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: Article XII-A grants an operative Licensor IP indemnity, carries all three customary exclusions (Licensee modifications, combinations with items not supplied by Licensor, Licensee specifications), imposes mandatory procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund fallback, and caps that indemnity at three times annual fees paid.

The two consequential edits to Article XIII are necessary, not extras: XIII(a) expressly barred any Licensor liability for infringement claims and XIII(b) capped Licensor at one half of amounts paid, either of which would have rendered the new indemnity and its 3x super-cap illusory. Each carve-out is drafted narrowly ("EXCEPT FOR LICENSOR'S INDEMNITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A") and no existing wording is deleted, so minimality holds.

No preferred-level content was smuggled in (no defence duty, affiliates, breach-of-law, data-breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, no narrowing of Article XII), and no survival tail, expense or damages boilerplate was added — consistent with a clean fallback-only proposal.

Preferred level is not reached and the finding should not be characterised as such: to move up, the drafter would need to add "defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensee and its affiliates", limbs for Licensor's breach of applicable law, Licensor-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee data, and Licensor's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, a notice/control/cooperation procedure, corresponding widening of the Article XIII(a) and (b) carve-outs beyond Article XII-A's IP-only scope, and a narrowing of Article XII to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law.

Residual tension to watch (not a defect in the selected checklist): retained Article XII still makes Licensee "solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights", which could be argued to circle back an infringement claim Licensor has just indemnified. A one-line opener to Article XII — "Except as provided in Article XII-A," — would remove the argument without expanding scope.

Severity remains critical as a finding: the unamended Agreement sits in walk-away territory (one-way Licensee indemnity plus an express bar on any Licensor infringement liability and a half-of-fees cap); the proposed language cures it to the fallback.
